Dots are personal AI agents developed by OpenAI , unveiled during the DevDay 2026 keynote in San Francisco on 29 September 2026. Built into ChatGPT and powered by the GPT-6 Astra model, Dots are part of the 2026 wave of personal AI agents that also included Meta's Muse , xAI's Grok Bot and the startup Instinct .

Unlike a chatbot that answers in a single exchange, Dots are always on, each running on its own cloud computer, and pursue user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight. A user can reach a dot from ChatGPT, text messages, Slack, Teams or a phone call, and OpenAI said users would eventually control several dots at once.

Dots can connect to more than 4,000 applications, including workplace tools such as Slack and Teams, to carry out tasks. In launch demos, a dot named Alfred ended a phone call by reporting that a user's website had gone live with the design already approved, and a dot named Felipe edited a company dashboard by voice and proactively flagged a scheduling clash

Dots (OpenAI)
Article History Edit
Dots are always-on personal AI agents from OpenAI, unveiled at DevDay on 29 September 2026, built into ChatGPT and powered by GPT-6 Astra.
Dots are personal AI agents developed by OpenAI , unveiled during the DevDay 2026 keynote in San Francisco on 29 September 2026. Built into ChatGPT and powered by the GPT-6 Astra model, Dots are part of the 2026 wave of personal AI agents that also included Meta's Muse , xAI's Grok Bot and the startup Instinct .
Concept
Unlike a chatbot that answers in a single exchange, Dots are always on, each running on its own cloud computer, and pursue user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight. A user can reach a dot from ChatGPT, text messages, Slack, Teams or a phone call, and OpenAI said users would eventually control several dots at once.
Capabilities
Dots can connect to more than 4,000 applications, including workplace tools such as Slack and Teams, to carry out tasks. In launch demos, a dot named Alfred ended a phone call by reporting that a user's website had gone live with the design already approved, and a dot named Felipe edited a company dashboard by voice and proactively flagged a scheduling clash between a finance meeting and a family event.
Availability
The first dot is included at no extra cost in OpenAI's Pro and Business Premium plans in eligible markets, with the Pro plan priced at $100 per month.

On September 28–29, 2026, OpenAI used DevDay to launch Dots , an always-on AI agent platform. Dots runs inside ChatGPT on the web and in the desktop apps, and it also works in Slack and Microsoft Teams ( OpenAI announcement , retrieved 2026-10-03). The short answer for IT: pilot it, don’t adopt it. The access model is bold, and OpenAI describes real admin controls. But prices for extra dots, outside benchmarks, and a security track record aren’t public yet.
Disclosure: The Back Room Tech has not tested Dots. Everything below comes from OpenAI’s announcement and third-party reporting, including The Verge’s October 2, 2026 hands-on, which we cite as a third-party source only.
What Happened
OpenAI’s Introducing dots post describes a Dot as an agent that keeps working toward a goal you set. It keeps going after you close the chat window. Here’s what OpenAI says each Dot does:
Runs on its own cloud computer and browser. Each agent gets its own environment, apart from your machine.
Connects to more than 4,000 apps. It can take actions across thousands of third-party services.
Runs on GPT-6 Astra, a model OpenAI named at launch.
Shows up where people already work: ChatGPT, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. There’s no separate Dots client to install.
Who this affects
According to OpenAI’s Meet dots documentation , access looks like this right now:
Plan | Dots access at launch | Notes |
ChatGPT Pro (Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500) | Users over 18 outside the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and Switzerland | First dot included at no extra cost |
Business Premium | Rolling out worldwide | First dot included at no extra cost |
Enterprise | Rolling out worldwide. Off by default ; a workspace admin must turn it on | No Enterprise Dots price listed |
OpenAI’s announcement says the first dot is included at no extra cost on Pro and Business Premium, and that adding more dots or paying for more speed or workload will come later, without published prices. OpenAI also says dots are rolling out gradually, so an eligible plan may not see them right away. For the first month only , conversations with a dot don’t count toward eligible Pro, Business, and Enterprise plan usage limits; work or Codex tasks a dot starts still use those products’ normal allowances. What happens to dot-conversation usage after that first month hasn’t been published — OpenAI says plan-specific terms will follow, so don’t plan a pilot budget around the introductory allowance staying permanent.
The enterprise pieces that matter to admins
Specialist Dots are the most interesting part for IT. OpenAI’s announcement is only a preview here: specialist dots with their own identity for access management , IT-provisioned hardware, and deep integrations with a company’s systems of record. OpenAI hasn’t published how those identities are created or scoped. If it works as described, that’s close to a managed service account. The agent doesn’t inherit one employee’s full login.
